title: demand_era binding is validated but never consumed — invariant (b) can check a different demand row than the one the director spawns from
evidence: core/demand.odin:52 `de := &cat.demand.eras[era-1]` (scripted_plan_demand keys the demand row off the era INDEX directly); core/catalog.odin:1232 `drow := &cat.demand.eras[de-1]` (the demand-subset invariant validates the BOUND row). A repo-wide grep for `demand_era` outside catalog.odin/catalog_test.odin/era_test.odin returns zero runtime consumers.
detail: If an eras.json row sets demand_era != era, the load accepts it and validates the bound row's classes against the roster, but the sim spawns from cat.demand.eras[era-1] — the invariant checked the wrong row. Latent today (all shipped rows have demand_era == era).
recommended_fix: Either fail-fast at load when demand_era != era (make the index convention explicit), or have scripted_plan_demand resolve the demand row via cat.eras[era-1].demand_era.

title: Sparse eras.json pads gap rows with empty Era_Row{} and the FSM validates an advance into a gap era
evidence: core/catalog.odin:1243 `for len(cat.eras) < int(era) { append(&cat.eras, Era_Row{}) }` (no contiguity check); core/catalog.odin:1352-1357 `era_row` returns `&cat.eras[era-1], true` for any era <= len(cat.eras) including empty padding; core/era.odin:52 `if c.to_era == 0 || int(c.to_era) > len(cat.eras) { return .Invalid_Era_Advance }`.
detail: With rows 1 and 3 only, era 2 is an empty padding row (era=0, no roster, no demand binding) yet era_row reports ok=true and era_advance_validate accepts to_era=2. Latent with the shipped contiguous table.
recommended_fix: Fail-fast on non-contiguous era rows at load, or reject rows whose padded era field is 0 in era_row / era_advance_validate.

title: era_record_run duplicates the existing health_record_run full-stream collector
evidence: core/era_test.odin:70 `era_record_run :: proc(s: ^Run_State, ticks: u64, cat: ^Catalogs) -> ([dynamic]u64, [dynamic]Event) {` collects the FULL unfiltered event stream + per-tick hashes; core/health_test.odin:40 `health_record_run :: proc(s: ^Run_State, ticks: u64, cat: ^Catalogs) -> ([dynamic]u64, [dynamic]Event) {` does exactly the same. era_record_run's only delta is `start := s.tick + 1` resume semantics, and its sole caller (test_era_advance_e14_deferred_by_crisis) passes a fresh run at tick 0.
detail: A fourth near-copy of the step-collect-hash loop (after record_run/crisis_record_run/sla_record_run/health_record_run); the resume-from-tick delta is never exercised. Test-only, and the codebase tolerates this pattern, so note-level.
recommended_fix: Reuse health_record_run in the E14 test, or hoist one shared full-stream collector and delete the per-domain copies.
